British Values
The Department for Education states that there is a need:
‘To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs’.
The Department for Education defines British Values as follows:
Respect for democracy and support or participation in the democratic process
Respect for the basis on which the law is made and applies in England
Support for equality of opportunity for all
Support and respect for the liberties of all within the law
Respect for and tolerance of different faiths and religious and other beliefs
We encourage our children to be creative, unique, open-minded and independent individuals, respectful of themselves and of others in our school, our local community and the wider world. We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British Society and to the world.
At Uplands Community Primary School, we uphold and actively promote British values in the following ways:
- Our school motto: Be Kind, Be Yourself, Be Part of our Community
Our 3 golden rules are:
Alongside our 3 core values, each class also discusses and sets its own rules that are clearly understood by all and seen to be necessary to ensure that every class member is able to learn in a safe and ordered environment.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged, and given the freedom to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. e.g. by signing up for extra-curricular clubs, choosing the level of challenge in some lessons and becoming increasingly more involved in child-led learning.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of Those with Different Faiths and Beliefs
Respect is one of the core values of our school. This can be seen and felt in our pervading ethos in school. The pupils know and understand that it is expected and imperative that respect is shown to everyone, whatever differences we may have and to everything, however big or small.
All of the above is embedded throughout the school and strongly promoted at break and lunchtime:

Welcome
Welcome to Uplands Community Primary School
I am delighted to welcome you to Uplands Community Primary School's website.
Uplands is a small, very inclusive primary school of just over 100 children right in the heart of Stroud; a bit like a village school in the town where everyone knows everyone. We are open from 08:55-15:25pm and run a breakfast club from 08:00-08:55 and an after school provision from 15:25-17:30pm 5 days per week.
Our school motto is: Be kind - Be Yourself - Be Part of our Community

Breakfast Club
If you need an earlier start in the morning, why not take advantage of our Breakfast Club?
Our Breakfast Club is extremely popular and is open from 08:00 to 08:55 every day. The cost per pupil is £5.00 per session and pupils will enjoy a healthy breakfast of toast, cereal, fruit and juice.
The Club is supervised by Mrs Caroline Cairns and supported by other staff. As well as having a healthy start to the day, pupils are able to have fun in a relaxed environment before starting their school day.
If you are interested in your child starting Breakfast Club, please complete the application form and return to the School Office.

School Clubs
This term we are running the following exciting clubs:
We run a huge variety of extra curricular clubs which have included Gardening, Athletics, Football, Art & Craft, ICT, Lego, Choir, Stencil, Ball-Games, Rounders, Model, Dance, Sewing and French. These are run by staff and they help make life in school more colourful and exciting.
We are always on the look out for new and exciting opportunities to enrich our children's curriculum, so please get involved and offer any skills you feel you have to make our school an even better place to be.
In addition to the afterschool clubs we also offer lunchtime clubs which include Gardening, Sports, Football, Art & Netball.

SEND
Please find below documents relating to SEND, including our Accessibility Plan and governors report.
The school's SEND co-ordinator is Miss Chloe Nicholas and can be contacted on Tel: 01453 762409.
We are pleased to share that our school is now working in partnership with Young Minds Matter Gloucestershire, a service that supports children and young people with their emotional wellbeing and mental health.
Young Minds Matter Gloucestershire provides advice, guidance, and specialist support to help children manage challenges such as anxiety, low mood, friendship difficulties, and other emotional needs. Their team works closely with schools, families, and professionals to ensure children receive the right support at the right time.
By working with Young Minds Matter, our school will be able to access professional advice, training, and early support strategies to help us better understand and respond to pupils’ emotional wellbeing. This partnership strengthens our commitment to creating a safe, supportive environment where every child feels listened to, valued, and able to thrive both academically and emotionally.
If you would like to find out more about the support available through this service, please speak to the school office.
